economy.summary: Her campaign platform says she will support policies that help working individuals and families keep more of what they earn, raise wages responsibly so full-time workers can make ends meet, support small businesses, expand workforce development and skilled trades training, and keep housing attainable for young families, seniors, and veterans.
economy.short: Supports raising wages, small businesses, skilled-trades training, attainable housing.

abortion.summary: Her campaign platform, under healthcare, says she will protect access to reproductive healthcare under Pennsylvania law; the site does not detail a more specific position on abortion.
abortion.short: Says she will protect reproductive healthcare access under Pennsylvania law.

education.summary: Her campaign platform supports fair and responsible public school funding, expanding career and technical education programs, strengthening special education services, and building partnerships between schools, employers, and community colleges.
education.short: Supports fair school funding, career-technical programs, stronger special education.

healthcare.summary: Her campaign platform proposes lowering prescription drug costs, strengthening rural hospitals and community health centers, and expanding access to mental health and substance use treatment.
healthcare.short: Proposes lowering drug costs, strengthening rural hospitals, expanding mental-health treatment.

energy.summary: Her campaign platform says she will encourage responsible energy development and job growth while maintaining strong environmental oversight, protect clean water and open space including Octoraro Lake and Big Elk Creek, and support farmland preservation.
energy.short: Encourages responsible energy development; protects water, open space, farmland.

guns.summary: Her campaign platform's public safety section supports law enforcement paired with accountability measures and promotes crime-reduction and rehabilitation policies; the site does not state a position on firearms specifically.
guns.short: Supports law enforcement with accountability; no stated firearms position.

economy.summary: His official biography highlights bipartisan legislation he introduced to support Pennsylvania's dairy farmers and to combat the invasive spotted lanternfly; it does not detail a broader economy or cost-of-living platform.
economy.short: Introduced legislation supporting dairy farmers; no stated cost-of-living platform.

taxes.summary: Chaired the Speaker's Debt Commission and authored Act 43 of 2019, which reformed how Pennsylvania issues debt to reduce interest costs; his biography says he opposes wasteful spending and notes he declines the state pension, per diems, and other legislative perks.
taxes.short: Authored state debt reform; opposes wasteful spending; declines perks.

abortion.summary: Voted in December 2021 for Senate Bill 106, a proposed constitutional amendment stating that the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right relating to abortion, including a right to taxpayer-funded abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: Says parents should be in charge of their children's education, not the government; authored legislation allowing parents to opt their children out of Keystone Exams and supports school choice and the Education Improvement Tax Credit program.
education.short: Supports school choice; says parents should direct children's education.

healthcare.summary: Has been active in bipartisan efforts to restore emergency health services in southern Chester County following local hospital closures.
healthcare.short: Worked to restore emergency health services after hospital closures.

guns.summary: Voted in November 2021 for Senate Bill 565, which would have allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a license; the bill passed the legislature and was vetoed by the governor.
guns.short: Voted for bill allowing concealed carry without a license.
